rationale: This is a MIN-mashup of the second legs of two already-evaluated signals ("R&D Gross-Surplus Liability Cover" and "Persistent R&D Cash-Flow Floor"), and because the two inputs are on incomparable scales — (revt−cogs)/lt is typically ~0.3–1.5 while TS_MIN(oancf/at) is ~0.0–0.1 — the MIN will almost always select the cash-flow floor, collapsing the signal into the archived Persistent R&D Cash-Flow Floor.

This is a straight SUMRANK blend of two already-tested archive signals ("R&D Maturity-Matched Financing" and "R&D Cash-Quality Liquidity") with no new economic content beyond averaging their second legs, i.e., a cosmetic combination rather than a substantively different hypothesis.

Although both legs share the lt denominator, txt/lt is mechanically an order of magnitude smaller than oancf/lt for most firms, so MIN() will be pinned to the tax term and the signal reduces to the already-evaluated "Tax-Paying R&D Solvency" rather than genuinely requiring dual confirmation.

Converting the archived level-based "R&D Cash Runway Commitment" into a five-year trend is a legitimate dynamics-versus-level distinction with a coherent forced-retrenchment mechanism and a sign that matches the expression's direction, though it remains a close relative of that prior signal and prior change-based R&D variants in the archive have generally been weak.

Since oancf is already net of cash taxes, subtracting txt/at converts (pi−oancf)/at into essentially standard total accruals, so the expression computes the Sloan accruals anomaly interacted with goodwill rather than the "tax validation" mechanism the hypothesis claims, and it barely differs from the archived "Goodwill Noncash-Earnings Quality Gap."

This is largely the sign-flipped counterpart of the archived "Purchased-Intangible Renewal Deficit" (NEG(xrd/at) becomes xrd/at on the same identifiable-intangibles base) with the second component swapped for che/act, which itself is the archived "R&D Cash-Quality Liquidity" leg, leaving little genuinely new to learn.
